knowledge_point.title: Calculating the Area of a Triangle Given Its Vertices

question.:question/problem:
Calculate the exact area of triangle $LMN$ with vertices $L(-1,-1,1)$, $M(-5,-3,-1)$, $N(-3,-1,-1)$, in square units.

Use two sides starting at $N$:
$$
\mathbf{u}=L-N,\qquad \mathbf{v}=M-N,\qquad T=\frac12\lVert\mathbf{u}\times\mathbf{v}\rVert.
$$

$T=$ {{area}}
question.:question/worked-solution:
Form two sides with the same starting vertex:
$$
\begin{aligned}
\overrightarrow{NL}&=\langle -1-(-3),-1-(-1),1-(-1)\rangle \\
&=\langle 2,0,2\rangle \\
\overrightarrow{NM}&=\langle -5-(-3),-3-(-1),-1-(-1)\rangle \\
&=\langle -2,-2,0\rangle
\end{aligned}
$$

Compute the cross product:
$$
\overrightarrow{NL}\times \overrightarrow{NM}=\begin{vmatrix}\mathbf{i}&\mathbf{j}&\mathbf{k}\\2 & 0 & 2\\-2 & -2 & 0\end{vmatrix}
$$
$$
\begin{aligned}
w_1&=0\cdot 0-2\cdot (-2)=4 \\
w_2&=2\cdot (-2)-2\cdot 0=-4 \\
w_3&=2\cdot (-2)-0\cdot (-2)=-4 \\
\overrightarrow{NL}\times \overrightarrow{NM}&=\langle 4,-4,-4\rangle
\end{aligned}
$$

The magnitude is the parallelogram's area:
$$
\begin{aligned}
\lVert \overrightarrow{NL}\times \overrightarrow{NM}\rVert&=\sqrt{4^2+(-4)^2+(-4)^2} \\
&=\sqrt{48}=4 \sqrt{3}
\end{aligned}
$$

The triangle has half that area:
$$
T=\frac12\lVert \overrightarrow{NL}\times \overrightarrow{NM}\rVert=\frac{4 \sqrt{3}}{2}=2 \sqrt{3}.
$$

knowledge_point.title: Calculating the Area of a Triangle Given Its Vertices

question.:question/worked-solution:
Form two sides with the same starting vertex:
$$
\begin{aligned}
\overrightarrow{DE}&=\langle -2-1,-1-(-2),2-(-1)\rangle \\
&=\langle -3,1,3\rangle \\
\overrightarrow{DF}&=\langle -2-1,-1-(-2),-1-(-1)\rangle \\
&=\langle -3,1,0\rangle
\end{aligned}
$$

Compute the cross product:
$$
\overrightarrow{DE}\times \overrightarrow{DF}=\begin{vmatrix}\mathbf{i}&\mathbf{j}&\mathbf{k}\\-3 & 1 & 3\\-3 & 1 & 0\end{vmatrix}
$$
$$
\begin{aligned}
w_1&=1\cdot 0-3\cdot 1=-3 \\
w_2&=3\cdot (-3)-(-3)\cdot 0=-9 \\
w_3&=(-3)\cdot 1-1\cdot (-3)=0 \\
\overrightarrow{DE}\times \overrightarrow{DF}&=\langle -3,-9,0\rangle
\end{aligned}
$$

The magnitude is the parallelogram's area:
$$
\begin{aligned}
\lVert \overrightarrow{DE}\times \overrightarrow{DF}\rVert&=\sqrt{(-3)^2+(-9)^2+0^2} \\
&=\sqrt{90}=3 \sqrt{10}
\end{aligned}
$$

The triangle has half that area:
$$
T=\frac12\lVert \overrightarrow{DE}\times \overrightarrow{DF}\rVert=\frac{3 \sqrt{10}}{2}=\frac{3 \sqrt{10}}{2}.
$$
